subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [See Nordstrom, Inc. v. Chubb & Son, Inc., supra, 54 F3d at 1435] (3) [3:713] Burden of proof: Several cases hold that while the insured must first demonstrate that a loss falls within the coverage of the policy, the burden then shifts to the insurer to demonstrate that the settlement amount was increased due to the liability of the corporation or an uninsured third party. [See Safeway Stores, Inc. v. National Union Fire Ins. Co. of Pittsburgh, Penn., supra, 64 F3d at 1288-1289; and Nordstrom, Inc. v. Chubb & Son, Inc., supra, 54 F3d at 1434] ➪ [3:714] PRACTICE POINTER: While insurers will often contend that all or most of the settlement or defense costs in a case should be allocated to the uninsured corporation, counsel for insureds (whether representing individual directors or officers or the corporation) may be able to resist such allocation based on the fact that covered claims against the directors and officers are intertwined with and inseparable from noncovered claims.
